channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Eisenkot Invites Netanyahu's Likud to Marathon Coalition Talks in Bid to Form Broad Government
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief tasked with forming Israel's next government, has invited Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party to marathon coalition talks starting on Sunday, in the clearest sign yet that he is trying to build a broad government that leaves Netanyahu out of the top job.

item.title: Turnout Falls as France Protests Enter Sixth Weekend, With Clashes in Marseille and Lyon
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched across France on Saturday for a sixth straight weekend of protests over the cost of living and public services, but turnout fell sharply from a week earlier as about 70,000 police officers were deployed and sporadic clashes broke out in several cities.

item.title: Trump Vows a Permanent Iran Deal That No Future President Can Undo
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he intends to secure a permanent agreement with Iran that would prevent Tehran from ever obtaining a nuclear weapon, and that no future American president should be able to reverse it.

item.title: Aoun Demands Israeli Withdrawal and an End to Iranian Meddling in Lebanon
item.description: Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun said on Saturday that his country cannot fully celebrate its independence while Israeli forces hold Lebanese land and foreign powers interfere in its affairs, in a speech that pressed both Israel to withdraw and Hezbollah to give up its weapons.

item.title: Pezeshkian Says Iran Faces 'Silent Economic War' Tougher Than Missile War
item.description: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday that his country is fighting a 'silent economic war' that is far more difficult than a military conflict, as the war with the United States and Israel squeezes its economy.

item.title: Iran Announces Rolling Power Cuts From Sunday as War Damage Strains Energy Grid
item.description: Iran will start scheduled power cuts on Sunday after strikes on its energy network during the war with the United States and Israel worsened a deepening electricity shortage, the head of the national power company has said.

item.title: Bahrain Rejects Iran's Claim It Hit US Radars and Asks UN to Act After Industrial Site Fire
item.description: Bahrain has rejected Iran's claim that its forces struck American air defence radars in the kingdom, saying the site hit on Saturday was a civilian industrial facility, and has asked the United Nations Security Council to act.

item.title: AOC Challenged Over Backing Jeffries as Speaker Amid Questions on His AIPAC Ties
item.description: CODEPINK co-founder Medea Benjamin confronted Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez over her support for Representative Hakeem Jeffries as the next House speaker, questioning his ties to the pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC and his record on Israel.

item.title: Blair Says Britain Should Only Rejoin a Reformed EU That Puts Technology First
item.description: Former prime minister Tony Blair has said Britain should only seek to rejoin the European Union if the bloc reforms to become more competitive on technology, arguing that returning to the EU as it stands today would be a mistake.

item.title: Trump Wants Ukraine Peace Deal by January as Zelenskyy Calls Summit a Failure for Putin
item.description: The Trump administration has told European and Ukrainian officials it wants Kyiv to reach a peace agreement with Russia by early January, before Democrats take control of Congress, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said this week's three-way summit had been a failure for Vladimir Putin.

item.title: 129 Bodies Recovered From Rubble in Central Gaza After 53-Day Search
item.description: Rescue teams in central Gaza have recovered the remains of 129 people from destroyed buildings, closing a search that ran for 53 days, Gaza's civil defence said on Saturday.

item.title: Iran Unveils New Twin-Missile Launcher at Underground Base as Guard Chief Warns Enemies
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard unveiled a new missile launcher on Saturday that it says can fire two liquid-fuelled missiles at the same time, during a tour of an underground missile base by its top commanders.

item.title: Iran Claims Its Air Defences Hit a US F-16 Over the Gulf; Washington Denies It
item.description: Iran's army said on Saturday its air defences launched a missile at an American F-16 warplane above the Persian Gulf on Friday evening, hitting the aircraft and forcing it to come down, a claim the United States military swiftly rejected as false.

item.title: Three Killed as Israeli Strike Hits Aid Vehicle in Gaza City
item.description: Three Palestinians were killed in Gaza City on Saturday when an Israeli strike hit a vehicle carrying food for the World Central Kitchen charity, just as it was about to hand out meals to children, according to Gaza's health ministry and witnesses.

item.title: Ebola Death Toll Passes 5,700 in Congo as WHO Keeps Global Emergency in Place
item.description: More than 5,700 people have now died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, the deadliest in the country's history, as the World Health Organization kept the crisis a global emergency and warned that the response still needs to grow.

item.title: US Says Russia Is Open to NATO-Style Guarantees for Ukraine, but Moscow Says No
item.description: American envoys say Russia has grown comfortable with the idea of NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine, but Moscow pushed back on Friday, saying even a formula resembling alliance membership is unacceptable, leaving the centrepiece of the US peace effort in dispute.

item.title: Finland Says Ukraine Likely Behind Drone Strike on Russian Cargo Ship as Crew Evacuates
item.description: Finland said on Saturday that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike that set a Russian cargo ship on fire in the Gulf of Finland, as the crew evacuated the burning vessel and a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating Finnish airspace.

item.title: Zelensky Calls Crimean Bridge Strikes a 'Fair Response' to 109 Russian Attacks on Ukrainian Bridges
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky has called Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge a fair response to Russia's attacks on Ukrainian bridges, saying Moscow hit bridges in Ukraine 109 times with missiles and drones.

item.title: Mexico Captures FBI Most Wanted Cartel Boss 'El Chapo Isidro' After Gun Battles in Sinaloa
item.description: Mexican forces have captured Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro', one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, after a military operation in the northwestern state of Sinaloa set off hours of gun battles, the country's defence ministry said.

item.title: Israeli Strikes Hit Southern Lebanon Towns as Border Attacks Continue
item.description: Israeli forces carried out a series of strikes across southern Lebanon on Saturday, hitting the towns of Qantara and Kfar Tebnit and setting off demolitions near Khiam, Lebanese state media reported, in the latest round of attacks along the border.

item.title: UN Talks Agree to Work on Rules for AI 'Killer Robots' by 2028
item.description: Countries at a United Nations conference in Geneva have agreed to spend the next two years working on rules for lethal autonomous weapons, systems that can pick and strike targets with little or no human control.

item.title: Verstappen Inherits Las Vegas Grand Prix Pole as Antonelli's Penalty Drops Him to Sixth
item.description: Max Verstappen will start the Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole position after the fastest qualifier, newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli, was handed a five-place grid penalty for an engine change.

item.title: Iran Says Reopening Hormuz Is 'Not Difficult' if US Accepts Its Terms
item.description: Iran's foreign minister says getting the Strait of Hormuz open again would be straightforward if Washington accepts conditions he called reasonable and in line with international law, as Tehran calls the American blockade an act of war and mediation through Qatar continues.

item.title: Iran Says It Downed Two US Drones Over Hormuz on Saturday, an MQ-9 and an MQ-1
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say their air defences brought down two American drones above the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, an MQ-9 Reaper in the early hours and an MQ-1 Predator over Qeshm Island later in the day, in the latest claims from the war.

item.title: Death Toll in Manipur Toxic Liquor Tragedy Rises to 13 as 346 Are Hospitalised
item.description: At least 13 people have died and 346 others are in hospital in India's north-eastern state of Manipur after drinking alcohol that officials suspect was tainted, police said on Saturday, as the toll from the suspected methanol poisoning climbed through the week and hospitals in the state capital filled up.

item.title: Iran Says a Tanker Hit a Mine and Caught Fire East of Hormuz After Two Vessels Were Struck
item.description: Iran's navy said on Saturday that an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz, hours after two tankers were hit by unidentified projectiles near the Omani town of Khasab, in the latest attacks on shipping leaving the strait.

item.title: Zelenskyy Calls Putin a 'Killer' After Trump Describes Russian Leader as His Friend
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called Vladimir Putin a 'killer' after US President Donald Trump described the Russian leader as his friend, exposing a public split over how to talk about Moscow as Washington presses for an end to the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $56,000 to Lowest in Two Years as $2 Billion in Bets Are Wiped Out
item.description: Bitcoin has fallen below $56,000 for the first time in more than two years, extending a steep slide that has erased over half its value since October, as a rout in technology shares and heavy selling by funds pushed the cryptocurrency through one support level after another.

item.title: South Africa's First Woman Deputy President, Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, Dies at 71
item.description: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first woman deputy president and the former head of the United Nations agency for women, has died at the age of 71, the presidency announced on Friday evening.

item.title: Iraq PM Orders Probe Into Basra Power Station Blast as Death Toll Disputed
item.description: Iraq's prime minister has ordered an urgent investigation into the gas pipeline explosion that set fire to the Hartha power station near Basra on Saturday, as officials and local reports gave conflicting accounts of how many people were killed.
